findings.checklist_item: Extend AC5 to require the verdict-string derivation (orchestrator.finalize_verdict and drift_floor._recompute_verdict_after_drop) to force INDETERMINATE on the new input_rejected signal, so an input-rejected degrade is never signed as a PASS.
evidence: finalize_verdict branch: `elif coverage.get('llm_unavailable'): verdict = 'INDETERMINATE'` (orchestrator.py:468) — this is what prevents signing a hollow PASS
_recompute_verdict_after_drop: `if cov.get('llm_unavailable'): verdict['verdict'] = 'INDETERMINATE'` (drift_floor.py:212)
gate_dispatch.py:203 & :560 catch LLMInputRejectedError in the SAME arm as LLMUnavailableError, both routing into _degraded_*_verdict which sets llm_unavailable=True unconditionally

AC5 text: 'coverage.llm_unavailable boolean is True only for genuine LLMUnavailableError outages; LLMInputRejectedError instead sets a distinct input_rejected signal' and readers are only 'updated to read it' — no INDETERMINATE-derivation requirement stated
findings.finding: AC5 removes coverage.llm_unavailable=True for LLMInputRejectedError but does not specify that the verdict-string derivation (orchestrator.finalize_verdict and drift_floor._recompute_verdict_after_drop) must force INDETERMINATE off the new input_rejected signal; today those branches key ONLY on llm_unavailable, so an input-rejected degrade could fall through to PASS and be SIGNED — the hollow-PASS invariant the flag currently protects.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria bullet 5 (coverage.llm_unavailable / input_rejected) + orchestrator.py:468, drift_floor.py:212
scenarios: A mid-run LLMInputRejectedError during review_plan: llm_unavailable now False, input_rejected True, but finalize_verdict has no blocking/other gate → verdict PASS → review_plan SIGNS an attestation with no LLM findings
findings.suggested_fix: State that finalize_verdict and _recompute_verdict_after_drop must treat input_rejected like llm_unavailable for INDETERMINATE derivation (an OR of both degrade-cause flags), so removing llm_unavailable=True for LLMInputRejectedError does not open a hollow-PASS path.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the total mapping of `degrade_cause_flags`: input_rejected for LLMInputRejectedError, llm_unavailable for LLMUnavailableError/LLMConfigError, and an explicit default (llm_unavailable) for every other LLMRunnerError subtype and the string-error tail, so the signal enum is total and no degrade leaves both flags unset.

findings.finding: The new `failure.degrade_cause_flags` helper's mapping is specified only for LLMInputRejectedError (→ input_rejected) and LLMUnavailableError (→ llm_unavailable); the plan does not state which flag the OTHER LLMRunnerError subtypes (LLMBudgetExhaustedError, ContextWindowExceededError, RunawayToolLoopError, StructuredOutputError/UnretryableOutputError/CompletionRecoveryError) and the string-tail degrade case receive.
findings.location: Acceptance Criteria, AC5 ('a shared failure.degrade_cause_flags helper'); Scope 'gate-degrade coverage.llm_unavailable boolean'

findings.finding: Child 7d47's body contradicts the parent's reconciled AC3 for the same WorkflowError caller-input family. 7d47 (as written) proposes routing the WorkflowError family to command_failed ('Minimal de-risk with existing vocab: route the WorkflowError family off llm_unavailable (e.g. to command_failed)') and treats the workflow-fault code as an open, escalated design decision, asserting 'invalid_input does not exist in this tree'. findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Align fbc0/f75f bodies with the parent's resolved taxonomy: derive error via error_code_for (which yields command_failed for the LLMRunnerError subtree) — no new vocabulary, no open escalation.

f75f: 'a richer per-type vocabulary would be a separate escalate'

findings.finding: Children f75f and fbc0 (as written) frame their remedies as unresolved escalations / needing-new-vocabulary decisions that the parent has already reconciled, creating a conflicting-assumptions mode. fbc0 says its fix 'needs a code-vocabulary decision consistent with error_code_for and the coverage.llm_unavailable flag -> escalate ... likely new vocabulary'; f75f notes 'a richer per-type vocabulary would be a separate escalate'. The parent forbids inventing new codes and fixes the exact routing (LLMRunnerError subtree -> command_failed) with existing vocabulary, so both children's 'needs decision / likely new vocabulary' framings are residual references to a pre-reconciliation state.
scenarios: An implementer following fbc0's body would block on a vocabulary decision the parent has already made (use command_failed via error_code_for), stalling AC2 or introducing a divergent new code contrary to the constraint
findings.suggested_fix: Update fbc0 to state the top-level error is derived from error_code_for(exc) per the reconciled taxonomy (no new code); drop the 'likely new vocabulary / escalate' framing in both children.
